raw_first_observations: One central vertical stack of white/gray fronts narrows toward the bottom in perspective.
The topmost object is cut by the top image boundary.
The central front regions are exposed; a bright vertical basket member is close to the left ends and lower basket members are close to the bottom object.
Bright projecting bands and rounded/soft edge transitions require distinguishing the target junction from adjacent structures.
record.semantics_used: Current confirmed two actual lower-front corners, ordered by image X; unlocatable endpoint must stay 0 0 0. No bounding-box extent policy was adopted.

findings.visible_facts: The upper part of the topmost front extends beyond the image boundary. The annotated long-edge junction itself is below that boundary: its left and right ends remain visible. The points lie at the transition between the broad gray front panel and the brighter projecting band below it, rather than on the image boundary or the basket rail.
findings.corner_assessment: No unambiguous wrong-edge, swapped-side, missing-visibility, or coordinate defect established. Top truncation does not by itself make these lower endpoints missing. The rounded right transition and blurred left transition do not support a uniquely exact subpixel corner.
findings.box_assessment: The box starts at y=0.167 px and includes the top-truncated front plus a bright lower band. Whether its bottom should be tightened is a box-extent convention question; no replacement rectangle is proposed.

findings.visible_facts: A distinct front directly below row 1 has a visible long lower junction and both terminal turns. The left point is adjacent to but on the object side of the bright vertical basket member; the right point is on the visible turn into the side boundary.
findings.corner_assessment: The existing points follow the same observable front/lower-edge junction as the other reviewed rows. No physically supported displacement or missing-point conversion is justified by this view.
findings.box_assessment: The box includes a band below the endpoint line and overlaps neighboring vertical extents. Box overlap alone does not establish duplicate objects or a labeling defect; no amodal/visible convention is adopted.

findings.visible_facts: The second-lowest labeled front is individually visible. Its lower horizontal junction meets the left boundary next to the basket member and the rounded right side. Both marked endpoints remain on visible object evidence.
findings.corner_assessment: No unambiguous corner defect. The left transition is narrow and soft near the bright rail, so a claim of one-pixel precision is not warranted. Neither point needs to be inferred behind an occluder.
findings.box_assessment: The rectangle extends below the long-edge junction and its left boundary includes some surrounding margin. The amount of margin/bright lower structure to include is unresolved, not an accepted correction.

findings.visible_facts: The bottommost labeled front has a visible lower junction above the basket crossbar. The right-hand white projecting feature continues below the annotated junction; the marked right point is at the front junction, not at the bottom of that protrusion. The left endpoint is visible just to the object side of the vertical basket member.
findings.corner_assessment: No supported reason to move the right point down to the protruding feature or the left point onto the basket crossbar. Existing visibility is supported. The soft contact region limits exact coordinate adjudication.
findings.box_assessment: The box includes the projecting lower feature down to approximately y=518.6 px. Whether that feature belongs in the box remains a semantic extent decision; the corner review does not settle it.

cases.raw_first_observation: The uppermost white front in the selected column is cut by the top image boundary. Its lower edge is visible as one continuous band. The next distinct front begins below the intervening seam; there is no second visible front within the selected pair region.
cases.subsequent_overlay_observation: Both row boxes cover that same uppermost partial front. Row 54 places its two visible points near the exposed lower-left and lower-right ends. Row 15 assigns both points unlocatable over the same physical front.
cases.decision_rationale: Retain row 54 as the existing representation with the visible corner pair; propose removing row 15 only after independent agreement that both rows identify this one front.
cases.coordinate_quality_limit: The front is only a narrow strip at the image boundary and is somewhat blurred. This review establishes instance correspondence, not an exact pixel-accuracy guarantee for row 54.

cases.raw_first_observation: The lowest white front of the middle-right column is partly hidden by the left gripper finger. Its exposed right section ends beside the basket divider. A separate front is visible above it, outside the overlapping bottom-front region.
cases.subsequent_overlay_observation: Rows 35 and 38 cover the same partly occluded bottom front. Row 38 preserves the hidden left endpoint as zero and places its visible right endpoint near the exposed lower-right end. Row 35 has two zero endpoints over the same front.
cases.decision_rationale: Retain row 38 with its one-visible/one-unlocatable state; propose removing row 35 only after independent physical correspondence agreement.
cases.coordinate_quality_limit: The gripper hides the left portion and the right edge is blurred. No hidden coordinate is inferred, and no separate coordinate or box refinement is justified by this bounded duplicate review.

cases.raw_first_observation: At the image top, one partial white front has a visible lower edge sloping downward toward the right. A second front lies below the clear seam. There are not two separate fronts corresponding to the two overlapping boxes.
cases.subsequent_overlay_observation: Row 21 covers the upper portion of that partial front and stops before its right-hand lower edge. Row 22 covers the same front through its exposed lower-right end, with both corner annotations visible. The distinct front below lies below the selected row 22 front.
cases.decision_rationale: Retain row 22, including its existing coordinate text; propose removing row 21 as the second annotation of the same front after independent agreement.
cases.coordinate_quality_limit: The lower edge is visible but soft. This review does not establish a specific endpoint-error tolerance or support moving the retained points.
